findings.title: IdP validates_token rule contradicts enterprise wrapper
findings.problem: The new Identity Providers section says an IdP declares validates_token = True only when its own authenticate() verifies the token signature. But EnterpriseIdpWrapper (src/codemie/enterprise/idp/dependencies.py:62) declares validates_token = True and passes the request headers to the enterprise provider. Its own comment says the deployment must verify the signature (JWKS validation or a validating gateway), which budget-attribution.md:39 also says. The section's Evidence line leaves the enterprise wrapper out.
findings.impact: The rule this guide states as an invariant is false for one of the three providers in the code. A reader who follows the guide could set the enterprise flag to False, which silently stops claim snapshots for enterprise sign-ins and breaks scheduled and webhook budget attribution. A reader could also assume any provider with the flag set is verified by the application, and misjudge the deployment's JWKS or gateway requirement.
findings.recommendation: Reword the rule so it matches the code: an IdP declares validates_token = True when its tokens are signature-verified, either by its own authenticate() (JwksValidatingIdp) or, for EnterpriseIdpWrapper, by the deployment (JWKS_VALIDATION_ENABLED or a validating gateway). Add the enterprise wrapper (src/codemie/enterprise/idp/dependencies.py:62) to the Evidence line and keep the header-trusting LocalIdp example as the case that must stay False.

findings.title: is_admin pinning advice incomplete with user management off
findings.problem: The Config-Derived User Flags section says a test that depends on is_admin must pin ENV and ENABLE_USER_MANAGEMENT, or it depends on what an earlier test left in config. With ENABLE_USER_MANAGEMENT pinned to False, resolve_is_admin (src/codemie/rest_api/security/user.py:152-155) still reads config.ADMIN_USER_ID and config.ADMIN_ROLE_NAME, and the guide does not tell the test to pin them. The cited fixture (test_cli_attribution_chain.py:86-87) avoids this only because it pins ENABLE_USER_MANAGEMENT=True.
findings.impact: Pinning both named settings, as the guide says, still leaves is_admin depending on config in the user-management-off branch that the guide itself describes. Tests written from the guide can stay order-dependent and flaky.
findings.recommendation: State that pinning ENV and ENABLE_USER_MANAGEMENT=True makes is_admin come from the value passed in. If a test pins ENABLE_USER_MANAGEMENT=False, it must also monkeypatch ADMIN_USER_ID and ADMIN_ROLE_NAME, because resolve_is_admin reads them in that branch. Optionally note that is_maintainer=True always forces is_admin=True.
